problem: "Each cell sees a 32×32 pixel region" confuses the stride (the 32×32 patch of the input that maps to each cell) with the receptive field. The receptive field of a cell in the final layer is much larger than 32×32 — it covers most of the image — because it is built from stacked 3×3 convolutions. A student will conclude the network only looks at a small window.
fix: Each cell corresponds to a 32×32 pixel patch of the input (its true receptive field is far larger), so the map is coarse: it knows what is present but not the exact boundary.

problem: "unless skips change the path" is vague and can be read as saying skips change the total upsample factor. In FCN-16s the total factor is still ×32 (×2 then ×16); skips only add detail at intermediate resolution.
fix: The total upsample factor must equal the total stride: five stride-2 pools give a ×32 total, so FCN-16s uses ×2 then ×16 (still ×32 in total), not ×32 from the coarse map alone and never ×16 in total.

problem: Grammar error: "The decoder unpool with those indices" — the verb does not agree with the subject.
fix: The saved max-pooling indices. The decoder unpool with those indices (unpools using those indices), so the upsampling step has no learned parameters.
